prompts.display_text: Pin a country home to an Old Testament outsider the New Testament mentions (not Balaam, the queen of the south or Sodom)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was home to an Old Testament person or people from outside Abraham's family whom the New Testament mentions (not Balaam, the queen of the south or Sodom)
prompts.citation: Luke 4:26-27; Matthew 1:5; 12:41; Hebrews 7:1; 11:31; Romans 9:17; Galatians 4:24-25; 2 Timothy 3:8; Matthew 1:6
prompts.note: Jericho is in the West Bank (PSE). Balaam's Pethor and the queen of the south's Sheba are disputed sites and are not counted.
prompts.summary: The New Testament keeps pointing to outsiders in Israel's story. Jesus praised Naaman of Syria, a widow of Sidon and the repentant Ninevites. Ruth of Moab and Rahab of Jericho appear in his genealogy, Melchizedek king of Salem in Hebrews, and Paul names Pharaoh, Hagar and the magicians of Egypt.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Paul names Pharaoh, Agar (Hagar the Egyptian), and the magicians Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses (Romans 9:17; Galatians 4:24; 2 Timothy 3:8).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus said the men of Nineveh, who repented at Jonah's preaching, would rise in judgment (Matthew 12:41).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Jesus recalled that Naaman the Syrian, of all the lepers, was cleansed (Luke 4:27).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Melchisedec was king of Salem, which the Bible Dictionary identifies with Jerusalem (Hebrews 7:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Ruth, a woman of Moab (Ruth 1:4), is named in Jesus' genealogy; Moab lay east of the Dead Sea (Matthew 1:5).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus recalled Elijah being sent to a widow of Sarepta, a city of Sidon (Luke 4:26).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: By faith Rahab of Jericho, a Canaanite, perished not with them that believed not (Hebrews 11:31; Joshua 2).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: The genealogy names Urias, Uriah the Hittite (Matthew 1:6; 2 Samuel 11:3); BD Hittites says their empire extended to the extreme northwest of Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding land allotted to a tribe of Israel in Joshua 13-19
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding land allotted to a tribe of Israel in Joshua 13-19, from Bashan and Gilead east of the Jordan to Asher's border at great Zidon and Judah's border at the river of Egypt
prompts.note: Jericho, Bethel and Hebron are in the West Bank (Palestine); much of Judah and the northern tribes lie in Israel.
prompts.summary: After the conquest, Joshua divided the land by lot. Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh took Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan, while the other tribes took Canaan, with Asher's coast stretching toward Zidon and Tyre and Judah's south border reaching the river of Egypt (Josh 13-19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Most tribes, including Naphtali, Zebulun, Issachar and much of Judah, were given land west of the Jordan (Josh 15-19).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Benjamin, Ephraim and Judah held land now in the West Bank, such as Jericho, Bethel and Hebron (Josh 15:54; 16:1; 18:21-22).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh received Gilead and the plains east of the Jordan (Josh 13:8-25).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Asher's border reached to great Zidon and the strong city Tyre (Josh 19:28-29).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Half of Manasseh received all Bashan, the kingdom of Og with Edrei and Ashtaroth (Josh 13:12, 29-31).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Judah's south border went out unto the river of Egypt, the Wady el Arish in northern Sinai (Josh 15:4, 47; Bible Dictionary).

prompts.display_text: Pin the homeland of a language (not Arabic) whose first Book of Mormon, whole or in part, came out in 1980
prompts.text_original: A country that is the home of a language, other than Arabic, in which the Book of Mormon was first published, in selections or in full, in 1980
prompts.citation: Church translations table, Book of Mormon; Church News, 27 Feb 2022; Global Histories chronology: Fiji
prompts.note: Arabic, also first published in 1980 as selections, is left out so the list stays closed. Russian is dated 1981 by Church News.
prompts.summary: The year 1980 brought the Book of Mormon into six new languages, mostly as selections that were completed later. Besides Arabic they were Bulgarian, Navajo, Ecuadorian Quichua, Vietnamese and Fijian, whose first 50 copies reached Suva that October.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Fijian, 1980; the first 50 copies reached Suva on 29 October 1980.

answers.name: Vietnam
answers.fact: Vietnamese selections came out in 1980 and the full book in 1982.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Bulgarian selections came out in 1980 and the full book in 1999.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Navajo selections came out in 1980 and the full book in 1998.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Quichua (Ecuador) selections came out in 1980 and the full book in 2011.
